# Skills

This page groups technical methods by domain. The focus is on skills connected to documented work or identifiable implementation evidence; it does not imply the same proficiency level across all topics.

## Software engineering

- **Python** — advanced practical experience reported; examples include modular application code, typing, automated tests, and maintainability.
- **Software design and quality** — separation of concerns, data validation, testability, and reproducible workflows.
- **Backend and tooling** — command-line interfaces, configuration, and modular Python packages, including the public Wiki Knowledge project.

## Data science and machine learning

Five years of professional Data Science work in the Qlik/Talend lab has included:

- Data analysis and statistical work
- Classical machine learning
- Experimentation, benchmarks, and model evaluation
- Model comparison, classification metrics, threshold analysis, and error analysis

Validation methodology, data leakage, calibration, uncertainty quantification, and generalisation are important areas of active technical consolidation. The portfolio does not imply independent mastery of every statistical or ML method; project-level evidence and explicit limitations take precedence over a list of skills.

## LLMs, NLP, and knowledge engineering

Professional work areas include LLM/NLP and generative AI. Current public technical evidence includes:

- Evaluation of hallucination-detection and fact-checking approaches
- Benchmark metrics, aggregation, and threshold studies
- LLM-assisted source ingestion and structured knowledge generation
- Markdown/YAML-based knowledge organisation, validation, and lexical search

Specific proficiency in retrieval-augmented generation, fine-tuning, LoRA/QLoRA, and advanced statistical evaluation should be judged from dedicated experiments rather than inferred from broad work-area labels.

## Scientific computing and environmental modelling

- Reduced-order modelling of passive-scalar transport and environmental dispersion
- Applied mathematics and scientific modelling
- Research-based work documented in the linked 2006 journal article and 2008 book chapter

Tools and frameworks are linked to the projects in which they are used. A dependency listed in a project is not, by itself, evidence of a fully implemented feature.
